messages.content: Compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. Return JSON only. Use only what the text explicitly establishes. Do NOT invent an unmentioned release, retrieval, transfer, extra grip capacity, hidden hand position, or other transition. Treat one hand or foot as one exclusive physical resource for independent actions: if it is explicitly occupied and the next action needs that same hand/foot for a different independent task, that is CONFLICT unless the next text explicitly frees, transfers, repositions, or reuses the same held object for that action. COMPATIBLE = the next action follows physically from the established state. CONFLICT = the next action requires an occupied body part/object/state to be incompatible at the same time, or reverses an established state without an explicit transition. UNSPECIFIED = the text truly lacks enough physical information to decide. Do not rescue a contradiction by imagining a possible off-screen action.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
Tomas holds the rope in his right hand and a pistol in his left.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
Tomas grabs a ladder rung with both hands without releasing either.

Return {"status":"COMPATIBLE|CONFLICT|UNSPECIFIED"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. The previous action: Tomas holds the rope in his right hand and a pistol in his left. So at that moment, his right hand is holding rope; left hand is holding pistol.

Next action: Tomas grabs a ladder rung with both hands without releasing either.

So he wants to grab a ladder rung with both hands while still holding rope (right) and pistol (left). That means each hand must hold the rung. But they are already holding rope/pistol. So unless he can hold rung in addition, but "without releasing either" implies he doesn't release rope or pistol. He can't have both objects at same time? The rung requires his hands to grasp it; if he's grabbing rung with both hands, each hand must be on rung. But they are already holding rope/pistol. So conflict: cannot hold rung and rope/pistol simultaneously unless the rung is held by other body part or he uses one hand for rung while still holding rope? The action says "both hands" so each hand grabs rung; but both hands are occupied with rope/pistol, no release. Thus conflict.

Thus status = CONFLICT.
